objective: Automatically run object recognition, LiDAR display repair, and quality-gated SPAR3D for completed scans; replay the preserved four-room evidence for A-102 Moffett.

checkpoints.task: trace existing pipeline and A-102 inputs
checkpoints.finding: New scans already queue recognition and texture builds. SPAR3D is an isolated room-6 script. A-102 is a stitched overlay with no uploaded evidence artifacts or recognition job; its last texture build predates LiDAR repair.

checkpoints.task: persist and run automatic SPAR3D stage
checkpoints.finding: Texture jobs queue a separate furniture job, openings of the texture endpoint recover missing work, and only quality-gated meshes replace display geometry. API tests: 249 passed; web tests: 192 passed; typecheck and changed-file lint passed.

checkpoints.task: replay A-102 recognition and patched rendering
checkpoints.finding: All 1,600 selected frames were recognized from cache with no new model requests. Revision 8 added 475 nodes. Cross-view voting and a category guard corrected false sofa/table relabels in revision 10 while preserving all 759 node identities, measured geometry, and the owner label. Replay is idempotent; 97 referenced crops resolve, and assessment and display export completed. The label-only revision reused patched texture build 19, which used 360 photos and has 29.0% directly observed color coverage.

checkpoints.task: run A-102 SPAR3D and verify viewer
checkpoints.finding: A representative per-class pass across all four captures evaluated 12 furniture candidates: 11 rejected by the display quality gate and one skipped for insufficient held-out photos. Zero meshes were accepted. The viewer URL remains the repaired LiDAR scan.glb; its 834,293-face GLB loads successfully. Authenticated browser inspection was unavailable, so the published database and artifact were checked directly.
